programmes.show_description: Dr Winchester and Mr Hyde: Major Winchester gets addicted to benzedrine after a long stretch in surgery. Meanwhile Radar sets up a mouse race competition.
Escape in Time: The Avengers attempt to track down criminals who have mysteriously vanished. Is the case linked to the deaths of secret agents and a Tudor mansion?
The Boyfriend: Henry takes an instant dislike to his daughter Julie's new boyfriend when the couple come to stay for the weekend.
Rumpole and the Official Secret: Rumpole defends a woman charged under the Official Secrets Act for leaking information about the British government's tea and biscuit expenditure!
An uplifting round-up of good news stories from the UK and around the world.
Friends: A lesson about true friendship is underscored by Jonathan's decision to appoint Jenny, an ostracised overweight girl, as a tutor to a troubled baseball star.
An uplifting round-up of good news stories from the UK and around the world.
A Special Love: Part 1: Jonathan and Mark try to persuade a young man with Down's Syndrome to take part in the Special Olympics. Scotty and Diane learn whether or not they can have children.
An uplifting round-up of good news stories from the UK and around the world.

A Song for Jason: Part 1: Jonathan and Mark become counsellors at a summer camp for children with cancer. They encounter an angry teenage athlete and a boy with an overprotective mother.
A Song for Jason: Part 2: Jonathan encourages Jason's dad, Miki, to get to know his son a little bit better, but Miki would much rather forget he has a son altogether.
Times of Change: An excited Mary Ingalls accompanies her father to the Chicago Grange Convention to surprise John Edwards.
My Ellen: After Ellen Taylor drowns while swimming on a hot summer's day with the Ingalls girls, her grief-stricken mother finds it impossible to accept.
The Handyman: Meddling Mrs Oleson starts tongues wagging when a handsome handyman stays in the Ingalls' barn while helping Caroline with house renovations.
The Revelation: Daisy accepts John-Boy's marriage proposal, and he brings his fiancée home to meet the family. But John-Boy learns a secret that she has been hiding.
Grandma Comes Home: Grandma is finally allowed to return home, but everyone is so protective of her that she no longer feels she is needed or has a place in the family.
Drink: Frankie stops Father Vincent Sheahan for drink driving. Meanwhile, Paul has his eye on Louis' rundown shack.
The Great Escape: When florist Brian Addis discovers he owes the taxman £40,000 in VAT, he decides to sell up and start a new life in the countryside with his wife and children.
After Robert leaves Eleanor at a seaside hotel following a break from the rigours of work at the Thrift, O'Neill joins her to continue their romantic affair, despite her father's disapproval.

Rumpole and the Judge's Elbow: Rumpole defends the owner of a chain of massage parlours charged with running disorderly houses.
Our Finest Hour - Part 1: Newscaster Clete Roberts returns to interview the members of the 4077th for an update on the war conditions from the perspectives of those enduring it every day.
Our Finest Hour - Part 2: Hawkeye reveals his sensitive side, a departure from his generally humorous persona, during the Clete Roberts interviews.
The Billfold Syndrome: Major Charles Winchester refuses to talk to anyone in the unit when he is denied a future medical position back in Boston. Hawkeye and BJ goad him mercilessly.
Jacko is flying high with Gaynor, an air stewardess, whose schedule threatens to ruin his image. Meanwhile, Lionel celebrates his extension of family, but for Veronica the party is over.
Sandra's new boyfriend, Roy Hooper, puts all his cards on the table when Jacko remembers his devious past. Lionel and Lesley find they miss Veronica about the house in more ways than one.
Veronica returns to the scene with a surprising proposition for Jacko. Meanwhile, Lionel wallows in self-pity, and Philip becomes the man his nanny said he would be.
Three Times Table: Robin annoys the owner of the steakhouse next door with his outdoor seating plans, who makes a takeover bid for 'Robin's Nest'. Robin's going nowhere without a fight.
Great Expectations: Vicky thinks she might be pregnant, delighting Robin and horrifying her father. Meanwhile, the restaurant's new fruit machine is proving to be a distraction for Albert.

Bless the Boy in Blue: Mark asks God to make Jonathan a police officer for a while. After 40 years, Jonathan becomes human only to realise the harsh realities of being a cop.
Cindy: An aspiring actress wants to be accepted for who she really is, not in the image her well-meaning dad tries to transform her into.
The Wolves: Laura and Andy find what they believe to be a stray dog caught in a trap with her two pups nearby.
The Creeper of Walnut Grove: Inspired by a fictional Scotland Yard detective, Andy and Laura attempt to bring the mysterious Walnut Grove chicken thief to justice.
To Run and Hide: Holding himself responsible for a friend's death and unable to face the man's heavily pregnant widow, a disheartened Doc Baker leaves Walnut Grove.
The Empty Nest: Part 1: The family mourns Grandpa's death. Meanwhile, Mary Ellen and Erin become roommates in Charlottesville. Part 1 of 2.
The Empty Nest: Part 2: The family mourns Grandpa's death. Meanwhile, Mary Ellen and Erin become roommates in Charlottesville. Part 2 of 2.
The Cat and Daddy G.: Father Sheahan hears an interesting confession. Grainne's pet goat suddenly becomes indispensable after meeting Avril's horse.
In at the Deep End: While the Addis family busy themselves adjusting to their new country lifestyle, they neglect to notice that something is troubling their youngest daughter, Molly.
During an intense 24-hour heatwave in the middle of London, temperatures and passions rise, whilst the Thrift copes with exhausted casualties from the local brewery.

Rumpole and the Bright Seraphim: Rumpole heads to Germany to represent a British soldier court martialled for the murder of a regimental sergeant.
None Like it Hot: Another heatwave has hit and it's affecting everyone, especially Klinger. As a result of the heat, he has come up with one of his most ingenious discharge schemes to date.
They Call the Wind Korea: A windstorm hits and everyone is busy securing items. Klinger and Major Winchester encounter an overturned truck with four wounded Greek soldiers inside.
Major Ego: Charles dramatically revives a dying patient, becoming even more insufferable than ever when a photo journalist from Stars and Stripes arrives to publicise the story.
